title: You Can't Comb a Hairy Ball: Where Earth's Wind Stops
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. The hairy ball theorem says that a continuous field of directions laid flat on the surface of a sphere must vanish at at least one point. So at any moment there is somewhere on Earth where the horizontal wind is zero. The episode goes from Poincaré's eighteen eighty-five work and Brouwer's nineteen twelve proof to the Euler characteristic. It explains why a doughnut can be combed flat while a sphere cannot, and shows the same rule at work in the whorl of hair on the crown of the head and in why fusion reactors are built in a ring shape.
